docs.text: Ucupaint Documentation ¶ What is Ucupaint? ¶ Ucupaint is a Blender addon that stacks images, textures, and color attributes into layers with mask and baking support. Requirements ¶ You need at least Blender 2.76 to use this addon, but more advanced features may only be available in modern versions of Blender (2.80 & above). Installation ¶ Go to GitHub release page and download an addon package according to your Blender version. Or if you're using Blender 4.2+, you can also download it from the extension platform Open Blender, go to Edit > User Preferences, select the Add-ons tab, press the Install button, browse to your downloaded addon zip file, and click Install add-on. Contribute ¶ Visit Ucupaint Github to access or contribute to the source code. Or visit Ucupaint Wiki Github to access or contribute to the source code of this wiki. Sponsor ¶ If you find the addon useful, you can sponsor the addon development here and get the Ucupaint Plus version of the addon. Discord Server ¶ You can join Ucupaint Discord to ask or discuss things related to Ucupaint. Locations ¶ You can find Ucupaint in the properties panel of the 3D Viewport and also in the Shader editor. Blender 2.80 and above ¶ For Blender 2.80 and above, it's in the Ucupaint tab. The tab is only visible when you select an object that can have a material (mesh, curve, etc). Ucupaint location in Blender 2.80 and above Blender 2.7x ¶ For Blender 2.7x, you should be using the Cycles render engine. The UI is only visible when you select an object that can have a material (mesh, curve, etc). Ucupaint locations in Blender 2.76 to 2.79 are only available if you're using Cycles

docs.text: Bake as Layer/Mask ¶ When creating a new layer or mask, there are options to bake various data as an image layer. Bake as Layer Menu Bake as Mask Menu The bake process can take a while depending on your system. You can see how it works in the video below. Bake Bevel Normal as an image layer Rebake ¶ After you edit the mesh or the scene, sometimes you want to rebake the layer. The easiest way to do it is by pressing the Rebake button in the layer/mask source panel. Rebake using Rebake Button Be aware if you already have baked data (Bevel Normal for example) and you want to bake the same data type again, the default behavior is Ucupaint will overwrite the already baked data. To disable this, you can disable the Overwrite option in the bake dialog box. Batch Rebake ¶ If you already have multiple baked data, and want to edit the mesh or scene again, rather than pressing the Rebake button one by one for each baked image, you can just press Rebake All Baked Images , this will rebake all baked layers/masks in the Ucupaint node. The process can take a while depending on how much data you already baked. Rebake AO and Bevel Normal at the same time using Rebake All Baked Images Button Baked Texture Types ¶ There are several texture types that can be baked to a layer: AO ¶ AO (Ambient Occlusion) can darken the valleys or creases of your mesh. You can use options such as distance and local only. AO Pointiness ¶ Pointiness will highlight the valleys and ridges of your mesh. Pointiness will use a 32-bit float image by default since it needs more precision. Pointiness Curvature ¶ Curvature is similar to pointiness, with different valley and ridges behavior. It uses 8-bit image by default so smaller file size. Curvature Cavity ¶ Similar to pointiness and curvature, cavity will show valleys and ridges but with darker grayscale levels. It also uses an 8-bit image by default. Cavity Dust ¶ Dust is similar to the cavity map but adds additional Z top normals to the mix. Dust Paint Base ¶ Sometimes also referred to as the Blizzard or Dota diffuse map. This bake combines a dirt map with a vertical gradient and top-facing normals with a highlight. Credit to Danyl Bekhoucha for the shader setup. This bake is a good starting point for character texture maps. Paint Base Thickness ¶ Thickness will bake the thickness of the mesh. Internally, it uses the inverted normal AO to achieve the thickness. Thickness Wireframe ¶ Wireframe will bake the wireframe of the mesh. Wireframe Bevel Normal ¶ Bevel normal map in tangent space. This will bake bevel on sharp edges. Bevel Normal Bevel Grayscale ¶ Grayscale bevel of the mesh. Bevel Grayscale Multires Normal ¶ This will bake the highest level of multires to a normal map. Bake Multires Normal Demo Multires Displacement ¶ This will bake the highest level of multires to a displacement/bump map. Bake Multires Displacement Demo Other Objects Normal ¶ This will bake the surface normal of other non-active selected objects to a normal map. Bake Other Objects Normal Demo Other Objects Color ¶ This will bake the color of other non-active selected objects to a color map. Other Objects Color Other Objects Channels ¶ This will bake the principled BSDF channels of other non-active selected objects to ucupaint channels. Selected Vertices ¶ This will bake the selected vertices to white color while other vertices will be black. This can be useful for masking. Bake Selected Vertices as Mask Demo

docs.text: Baking Ucupaint Node ¶ Ucupaint node can be baked into images or color attributes, it's very useful if you want to export for another software. To bake ucupaint node, you can click on bake target popover button and click Bake Ucupaint Node . Bake Ucupaint Node button Press Bake Ucupaint Node will show up the bake settings of the node Bake Ucupaint Node dialog box The dialog box options for Bake Ucupaint Node will be applied to all bake targets that use the node settings. It can be individually set to custom settings if needed in the bake target settings. The settings for baking ucupaint node are: Resolution : Resolution of the baked image. Interpolation : Pixel filtering interpolation of the baked image. The default is linear, but use Closest for pixel art Samples : Sample for the baked image, the default is using one sample, it's generally fine, but try to increase it if the bake result has jagged lines or noises. AA Level : Supersample anti-aliasing level, you can only choose between 1 or 2. One is not using supersample anti-aliasing, and two (2) will quadruple the bake image size, and it will automatically resize back to the selected resolution, this can give good anti-aliasing in some cases, but very heavy on memory as it can cause crash if you run out of memory. Margin : Number of color pixels spread along the edge of UV islands to hide the UV seams, please increase it if the seam of your model looks visible in the far distance. Use UDIM Tiles : Use UDIM for the baked image. This will be enabled automatically if there are UV islands outside the 0.0-1.0 range (can be disabled in addon preferences) Use FXAA : Use FXAA antialiasing method as an alternative to the supersample one, it's very lightweight but can add slight blur in some texture details. Use Denoise : Use Blender denoising on the bake result, it can reduce noise if you use a realtime AO layer/mask Use Dithering : Use Blender dithering on the bake result, it can reduce banding if you use a gradient layer/mask. Force Bake All Polygons : This will bake all polygons even if the polygons don't use the active material. Useful if your material is a secondary material used in a Solidify modifier for example. Bake Disabled Layers : This will make all disabled layers enabled while baking the node. Only Necessary Channels : This will only bake channels that have at least one layer using (Base Layer is not counted, unless it's connected with an external node) Bake Device : Choose between CPU, GPU, or CPU (OSL) for the baking device. The GPU is usually faster, but it can hang the first time you do it for shader compilation. The OSL is useful to bake the most complex layer/shader setup if CPU and GPU fail to bake. After baking, the UI will switch to Use Baked UI, this will show you all the baked bake targets. Explanations for Use Baked UI You can toggle between Use Baked state of the node and the layered ones. Baking Ucupaint node demo The button labeled Outside beside the Use Baked button is used to move all baked nodes outside the Ucupaint node. This is useful for exporting the models with GLTF or FBX, which need the textures to be directly connected to the Principled BSDF. Use Baked Outside will make the baked nodes outside of Ucupaint node Bake Target ¶ Bake target is the setting for the image or color attribute that will be used for baking the ucupaint node. A channel needs a bake target to be able to be baked when you bake the ucupaint node. By default, when a channel is created, it always also creates a bake target for it. A bake target can be an image or color attribute. Bake target settings ¶ Bake target settings The settings for each bake target are: Channel : You can set the R , G , B , and A of the image channel to refer to which channel of Ucupaint. 32-bit Float : More precision for the image created, this option is only available for image bake target. Bake Settings : Bake settings like resolution, interpolation, etc. The default will use Use Node Settings , which means it will use the setting that is shown when you do Bake Ucupaint Node . If some special channel types are used for the bake target, there are extra bake target options: Normalize Height : Only available for height channel, if enabled, the bake result will fit into 0.0-1.0 range. Normal includes Height : Only available for the normal channel, if enabled, the height bump will be included in the normal map. Create new bake target ¶ To create a new bake target, press the + button beside the bake target list. New bake target dialog box The options for creating a new bake target are: Type : Choose between image or color attribute bake target Channel : Channel that will be used for the bake target. Use Custom to manually set the individual R , G , B , and A image/attribute channel of the bake target Preset : Only available when the Custom channel is selected, the only options available for preset right now are ORM and DirectX Normal. 32-bit Float : More precision for the image created, this option is only available for image bake targets. Example of creating a color attribute bake target and baking it

docs.text: Channels ¶ Accessing Channel Settings ¶ While a layer can also have channel settings, global channel settings can be accessed in the channel button above the layers list. Clicking the channels button above the layers list will show the channel settings list Blender 2.7x has the channel settings below the layers list, but you can also use this UI in modern Blender versions (2.80+) if you enable Use Non-Popup Channels and Bake Targets UI in the preferences. Channel in Ucupaint ¶ A channel in Ucupaint represents a pair consisting of an input and an output within the Ucupaint node. The Ucupaint channels input and output (I/O) on the actual node Each channel has at least one input and one output, except for the Height channel, by default it doesn't have an output (read Displacement Setup for more info). The base color or value of the channel is the default input of the node. They can be accessed through the channels list or on the base layer. Channel base values correspond to the node’s default input All inputs and outputs can be freely connected, allowing the Ucupaint node to work with your custom node setups. In the channels list panel, you can perform basic actions such as adding, moving up/down, or removing channels. Channels list panel Add New Channel ¶ To add a new channel, use the + button next to the channel list. There are a few options to choose, which are Custom , Alpha , Ambient Occlusion , Emission , Height , Normal , and Vector Displacement . The video below demonstrates how to create an Emission channel in Ucupaint. Notice that after creating a new channel, the Ucupaint node will display new input and output sockets corresponding to that channel. Adding an emission channel Add custom channel ¶ If you want to create a custom channel other than the default ones (Alpha, Emission, etc.), you can choose Custom , it will give you more options on what the channel output will be connected to and the data types. New custom channel dialog box The options when creating a new custom channel are: Name : Name of the new channel, automatically updated if you change the Connect To value to match the selected socket name. Connect To : Which socket the channel output will connect to. It lists all the unconnected sockets available in the material nodes. Type : Type of the channel, automatically updated if you change the Connect To value to match the selected socket type. Color Space : Colorspace of the channel, use non-color data if the channel is not used for its color appearance. Use Clamp : Limit the channel output to a minimum of 0.0 and a maximum of 1.0. Ignore Unconnected Warning : By default, Ucupaint will give you a warning if the channel doesn't connect to any other socket in the material nodes, this option is to bypass that. Set Strength to One : Only available on some selected sockets that have a parent strength value (example: Emission Color). Since the default strength is usually zero, this option is to set the value to one. Main Channel Types ¶ There are three main channel types in Ucupaint: RGB , Value , and Vector . Color is an example of a RGB channel, Metallic, Roughness, and Height are examples of Value channels, and Normal is a Vector channel. Channel Settings ¶ The channel settings for the selected channel can be accessed under the channel list. Example of RGB channel settings Here are the options available in the channel settings: Background/Base Value : The node input value of the channel, it is also accessible in the Base Layer and beside the channel name in the channel list. Use Clamp : Limit the value output of the channel to the 0.0-1.0 range. Space : Color space of the channel, use Color Data for channels that will be used for color, and Non-Color Data for channels that will be used for non-color purposes. Bake Target : The bake target that will be used as the data when baking the Ucupaint node. Special Type : This option will show up in certain channel, this is to set the channel as a special channel explained in the Special Channel Types section Special Channel Types ¶ There are special channel types in Ucupaint that do more than regular channels. In version 3.0, the special channel types are Alpha , Height , Normal and Vector Displacement . Alpha channel ¶ Alpha channel needs to be paired with a color channel to work effectively. Alpha channel also uses special blending that make sure the final color is rendered correctly. Specific settings available in the alpha channel are: Channel Pair : Links a color channel with the alpha channel. When the color channel is enabled on a layer, the alpha channel is automatically activated as well. Backface Mode : Option to hide the backface or frontface of the object. Normal channel ¶ Normal channel is a special channel that outputs world-space normals of the object surfaces. Specific settings that are available in the alpha channel are: Main UV : UV Map that will be used for calculating tangents, which are needed for Overlay blending mode Height channel ¶ Height channel by default will be used as bump if there's a normal channel and the Displacement Setup isn't enabled yet. Specific settings that are available in the height channel are: Normalize Input Output : This will normalize the height channel output to fit in the 0.0-1.0 range. It will also create a midlevel input that can control the midlevel of the height input. Displacement Setup : Displacement setup is just a status label. If you do the Quick Displacement Setup , this will enable the displacement setup, meaning the height output will be accessible and it's automatically connected to the displacement node. Vector Displacement channel ¶ Vector displacement channel is similar to the height channel, but rather than just using up and down height, it can use vectors to displace the object's surface Specific settings available in the vector displacement channel are: Displacement Setup : Similar to height channel, but whether displacement setup is enabled or not, the output of Vector displacement is always accessible. It just indicates that displacement setup has been done before, more details are in the Displacement Setup section Displacement Setup ¶ By default, Height channel in Ucupaint is for the bump effect on the normal channel, but it can also work with real displacement, you only need to do displacement setup first. For the Vector Displacement channel, it is designed to work with displacement setup enabled, since the channel can work as sculpt layers ( TODO: more info about that is on a different page ) Quick Displacement Setup ¶ The ' Quick Displacement Setup ' button is available on both Height and Vector Displacement channel settings. Quick Displacement Setup Options Options that are available for Quick Displacement Setup : Method : To set the displacement method of the current active material. Max Polygons : Will set the subdivision surface or multires modifier levels based on Max Polygons number. The input is in thousands, so 1000 means 1 million polygons. Adaptive (Cycles Only) : Will enable adaptive subdivision that only works on the Cycles renderer. This can improve displacement details, but will increase load time when entering render view. Dicing Rate : Will appear if adaptive is enabled. Dicing rate is the number of pixels on screen that will determine mesh subdivision. Doing displacement setup will also do these things: Add a subdivision surface modifier to all objects that share the material if there's no subdivision surface modifier yet. Set the subdivision level to reach the Max Polygons input. Notice that the input is in thousands , so 1000 means 1 million polygons. If the object already uses a multires modifier, it will set the levels of the multires modifier instead. If the model is detected using flat shading, the subdivision modifier will use the Simple type, otherwise it will use Catmull-Clark type subdivision. Set the displacement method of the material to the chosen method option, the default is Displacement and Bump so the height or vector displacement channel can actually displace the surface. By default, if there's a height and normal channel, the height channel output is not accessible. Doing a displacement setup will make it available. Create a displacement node if there's a height channel exists and connect the output of the height channel to the displacement node. Create a vector displacement node if there's a vector displacement channel exists and connect the output of the vector displacement channel to the vector displacement node. The displacement and vector displacement node will connect to the active material output, and if there are both of them, an Add Vector node will be added. All the displacement nodes will only be added if they don't exist yet, so it's safe to do Quick Displacement Setup multiple times to set the target polygons Necessary displacement nodes will be created after doing Quick Displacement Setup Remove Displacement Setup ¶ To remove the displacement setup, there's a button beside the quick displacement setup that has the X icon. Remove Displacement Setup Options The action input will give you three options: Recover Original State : This will keep or remove the subdivision modifier based on the first time you did the Quick Displacement Setup Remove Subdivision Modifier : Will remove any subdivision modifiers that exist on all objects that shared the active material. Keep Subdivision Modifier : Will keep subdivision modifiers, and there's an option to set subdivision level. Other than doing actions to the subdivision modifiers, removing the displacement setup will also do these things: Set the displacement method of the material to Bump Only so there will be no displacement on the surface If there's a height and normal channel, the height output is no longer accessible Displacement Demo ¶ The video below demonstrates displacement setup in action. Example of RGB channel settings Here are the options available in the channel settings: Background/Base Value : The node input value of the channel, it is also accessible in the Base Layer and beside the channel name in the channel list. Use Clamp : Limit the value output of the channel to the 0.0-1.0 range. Space : Color space of the channel, use Color Data for channels that will be used for color, and Non-Color Data for channels that will be used for non-color purposes. Bake Target : The bake target that will be used as the data when baking the Ucupaint node. Special Type : This option will show up in certain channel, this is to set the channel as a special channel explained in the Special Channel Types section
docs.title: Channel Settings

docs.text: There are special channel types in Ucupaint that do more than regular channels. In version 3.0, the special channel types are Alpha , Height , Normal and Vector Displacement .
docs.title: Special Channel Types

docs.text: Alpha channel needs to be paired with a color channel to work effectively. Alpha channel also uses special blending that make sure the final color is rendered correctly. Specific settings available in the alpha channel are: Channel Pair : Links a color channel with the alpha channel. When the color channel is enabled on a layer, the alpha channel is automatically activated as well. Backface Mode : Option to hide the backface or frontface of the object.
docs.title: Alpha channel

docs.text: Normal channel is a special channel that outputs world-space normals of the object surfaces. Specific settings that are available in the alpha channel are: Main UV : UV Map that will be used for calculating tangents, which are needed for Overlay blending mode
docs.title: Normal channel

docs.text: Height channel by default will be used as bump if there's a normal channel and the Displacement Setup isn't enabled yet. Specific settings that are available in the height channel are: Normalize Input Output : This will normalize the height channel output to fit in the 0.0-1.0 range. It will also create a midlevel input that can control the midlevel of the height input. Displacement Setup : Displacement setup is just a status label. If you do the Quick Displacement Setup , this will enable the displacement setup, meaning the height output will be accessible and it's automatically connected to the displacement node.
docs.title: Height channel

docs.text: Vector displacement channel is similar to the height channel, but rather than just using up and down height, it can use vectors to displace the object's surface Specific settings available in the vector displacement channel are: Displacement Setup : Similar to height channel, but whether displacement setup is enabled or not, the output of Vector displacement is always accessible. It just indicates that displacement setup has been done before, more details are in the Displacement Setup section
docs.title: Vector Displacement channel

docs.text: By default, Height channel in Ucupaint is for the bump effect on the normal channel, but it can also work with real displacement, you only need to do displacement setup first. For the Vector Displacement channel, it is designed to work with displacement setup enabled, since the channel can work as sculpt layers ( TODO: more info about that is on a different page )
docs.title: Displacement Setup

docs.text: The ' Quick Displacement Setup ' button is available on both Height and Vector Displacement channel settings. Quick Displacement Setup Options Options that are available for Quick Displacement Setup : Method : To set the displacement method of the current active material. Max Polygons : Will set the subdivision surface or multires modifier levels based on Max Polygons number. The input is in thousands, so 1000 means 1 million polygons. Adaptive (Cycles Only) : Will enable adaptive subdivision that only works on the Cycles renderer. This can improve displacement details, but will increase load time when entering render view. Dicing Rate : Will appear if adaptive is enabled. Dicing rate is the number of pixels on screen that will determine mesh subdivision. Doing displacement setup will also do these things: Add a subdivision surface modifier to all objects that share the material if there's no subdivision surface modifier yet. Set the subdivision level to reach the Max Polygons input. Notice that the input is in thousands , so 1000 means 1 million polygons. If the object already uses a multires modifier, it will set the levels of the multires modifier instead. If the model is detected using flat shading, the subdivision modifier will use the Simple type, otherwise it will use Catmull-Clark type subdivision. Set the displacement method of the material to the chosen method option, the default is Displacement and Bump so the height or vector displacement channel can actually displace the surface. By default, if there's a height and normal channel, the height channel output is not accessible. Doing a displacement setup will make it available. Create a displacement node if there's a height channel exists and connect the output of the height channel to the displacement node. Create a vector displacement node if there's a vector displacement channel exists and connect the output of the vector displacement channel to the vector displacement node. The displacement and vector displacement node will connect to the active material output, and if there are both of them, an Add Vector node will be added. All the displacement nodes will only be added if they don't exist yet, so it's safe to do Quick Displacement Setup multiple times to set the target polygons Necessary displacement nodes will be created after doing Quick Displacement Setup
docs.title: Quick Displacement Setup

docs.text: To remove the displacement setup, there's a button beside the quick displacement setup that has the X icon. Remove Displacement Setup Options The action input will give you three options: Recover Original State : This will keep or remove the subdivision modifier based on the first time you did the Quick Displacement Setup Remove Subdivision Modifier : Will remove any subdivision modifiers that exist on all objects that shared the active material. Keep Subdivision Modifier : Will keep subdivision modifiers, and there's an option to set subdivision level. Other than doing actions to the subdivision modifiers, removing the displacement setup will also do these things: Set the displacement method of the material to Bump Only so there will be no displacement on the surface If there's a height and normal channel, the height output is no longer accessible
docs.title: Remove Displacement Setup

docs.text: Layer ¶ Ucupaint UI is centered around the layers. After creating a Ucupaint node, Ucupaint UI will show the layer list with the Base layer as the first layer. Layers list of Ucupaint. It will have at least a base layer Base Layer ¶ The base layer is the channel input values of the Ucupaint node, which can also be accessed in the channel settings . Base layer is always at the bottom of the layer stack and can't be removed. Base layer demo Add New Layer ¶ You can add new layers by pressing the + button. There are various layer types that can help you finish your texturing process. Add layer menu If you choose Image > New Image , a dialog box will appear. New Image Layer Options ¶ New image layer dialog box Here are the explanations of the options when creating a new image layer: Name : Name of the layer, which is also the name of the created image. Channel : Channel that will be used by the layer. Resolution : Resolution of the created image. 32-bit Float : More precision for the image created, useful for painting height, but will use a lot more disk space. Interpolation : Pixel filtering interpolation that will be used for the render. Choose Closest if you want to create pixel art textures and Cubic if you want to paint the height. Everything else will be enough by using the default Linear . Mapping : Texture Mapping method that will be used for rendering. Use UDIM Tiles : Create UDIM tiles based on the UV Map chosen. This will automatically be enabled if you choose a UV map that has UV islands placed outside the 0.0-1.0 range. To disable this automatic UDIM detection, you can disable Enable Auto UDIM Detection in addon preferences. (*TODO: More explanation about UDIM in separate page *) Use Image Atlas : Use a shared image atlas image for multiple layers and masks. This is to circumvent the maximum image limit of Blender's OpenGL renderer mentioned in Pink Material page Painting an Image Layer ¶ After creating a new image layer, you can start painting to the image layer by going to Texture Paint mode. You can do that by changing Object Mode to Texture Paint on the Blender viewport menu or by pressing Ctrl+Tab and choosing Texture Paint . Example of creating image layers and painting them Layers in Ucupaint work like layers in any other image editing software. So if we create another layer and draw over it, it will cover the layer below. Reordering Layers ¶ You can reorder the active layer by clicking the arrow buttons beside the layer list. Reordering layers Saving the Image Layers ¶ After you paint a layer, you'll notice that there is an asterisk beside the layer name, that means the image is edited and haven't been saved yet. If you save the blend file, all images used in Ucupaint will automatically be saved or packed inside the blend file. In Blender 5.2 or newer, there is a prompt to tell you there are unsaved images, but whether you choose to click the toggle or not, when saving the blend file, Ucupaint will always save all the images used in Ucupaint node(s). Asterisk icons mean images are edited but not saved yet Packed icons mean images are packed in the blend file Layer Parameters And Options ¶ Layer Visibility ¶ The eye icon in the layer list is used to set the layer visibility. Toggling layer visibility on and off Layer Opacity ¶ Layer opacity is controlled by the slider on the left of the layer visibilty icon. Layer opacity slider in action Layer Mapping ¶ A layer will use UV mapping by default, but you can change it to another mapping type. Types of layer vector Be aware that if you're using a dynamic mapping like camera or window, the baked channel images will still be static. Mapping Transformation ¶ You can transform your mapping using translate, rotation, and scale sliders. Mapping transformation demo Mapping transformation is only available for non-decal mapping. Layer Source ¶ You can change the layer source to a different one and retain its mask and modifier settings. Use this button to change the layer type. Change layer type options Renaming Layer ¶ To rename a layer, double-click the name of the layer in the layer list and type the name of the layer. If your layer is an image layer, you'll actually also be renaming your image name. Renaming layer If you already learnt about masks, make sure you select the active data to be the layer, otherwise you'll be renaming the mask or custom data. Layer Special Menu ¶ Layer special menu can be accessed below the layer move up & down button. It contains many operators contextual to the selected layer and selected image data. Layer Special Menu Merge Layers ¶ There are two operators for merging layers, Merge Layer Up and Merge Layer Down . Currently, this only works with an image layer as the active layer. The merging process is using blender bake system internally so it can take a while if you're using large resolution and UDIM. The options for merging layers are: Main Channel : Channel for merge reference, you can only choose one. Apply Modifiers : This will apply the modifiers in the active layer. Apply Neighbor Modifiers : The merge process will include the modifiers of the neighbor/other layer for the merging. Duplicate Layer ¶ There are two operators for duplicating a layer, Duplicate Layer is for duplicating a copy of the active layer with all the pixel data if it's an image layer, all the mask pixel data (if there's an image mask) and all the modifiers and settings. Duplicate Blank Layer will duplicate the layer with all the modifiers and settings, but all the layer and mask pixel data will be blank. The options for duplicating a layer are: Duplicate Packed Images : Only available if there's packed image data in the active layer. This will duplicate the packed image into a new image, disabling this will reuse the image data in the duplicated layer. Duplicate Images on disk : Only available if there's an image sourced externally from disk in the active layer. Enabling this will duplicate the actual image into a new file on disk. Copy & Paste Layers ¶ There are two copy layer operators, Copy Layer will only copy the active layer and Copy All Layers will copy all layers in the active Ucupaint node. You can only paste the layer in the same blend file opened, as you cannot paste the layer in different blender instance for example. For pasting the layer, there's Paste Layer and Paste Blank Layer(s) , paste blank behaves similarly to duplicate blank, it will paste the layer with all the settings and modifiers, but the image data will be blank. There will be also option similar like duplicate like Duplicate Packed Images and Duplicate Images on disk depending if there are packed images or ondisk images. Also, if there's a copied baked image layer/mask, there will be an option to Rebake Baked Images , so if the layer is pasted to objects with different shapes, you can immediately rebake the images. Extra Operators ¶ Rebake All Baked Images ¶ The operator Rebake All Baked Images will rebake all baked image layers and masks. More explanation can be found in the bake as layer/mask page Refill UDIM Tiles ¶ If you already have many image layers/masks that use UDIM and want to add new UDIM tiles since you modified the UV Map, you can use Refill UDIM Tiles to quickly add new UDIM tiles based on the new UV Map. ( TODO: Dedicated explanation about UDIM workflow in Ucupaint ) Contextual Image Operators ¶ Some operators in the layer special menu are only applied to the selected active image data. Those operators are Resize Image , Invert Image , Pack Image , Save Image , and Convert Image . Convert Image ¶ In Convert Image submenu, there are some operators that you can use to convert images. Convert to Float/Byte Image : You can convert to a high/lower precision image. Convert to UDIM/Non-UDIM Image : You can convert the active non-UDIM image to become a UDIM image or vice versa Convert to Image Atlas : Convert the active image to use an image atlas so it will share image data to other image layers and masks. Or convert back to a standard image from an image atlas. Convert All Images to Image Atlas : Convert all images used in the current Ucupaint node to use image atlas. This will only be applied to packed images and images that have no transformation mapping. Export Layers as PSD ¶ Exporting to PSD layers is currently only available in Ucupaint Plus. More explanation about this can be found in the dedicated page . Layer Types ¶ There are several layer types that can be used in Ucupaint. Image ¶ Other than creating a new layer image explained here , you can also open an image from disk, or open an existing image in the current blend file. ( TODO: Open Image from materials/Open images to single layers explanations ) Color Attribute ¶ Color attribute can be used as a layer. There's also a special color attribute editor in edit mode. Adding a new color attribute layer and editing it in edit mode You can assign selected vertex/polygons to a certain color in edit mode. There will be buttons to assign them with White , Black or a custom Color . The color assigned in vertex select mode will bleed through all the corners of the connected polygons. In polygon select mode, the assigned color will only affect the selected polygons. Solid Color ¶ Solid Color layer contains only a single color and can be useful if you want to paint the mask first, then edit the solid color later. Solid color layer demo Geometry types ¶ Fake Lighting ¶ Fake lighting will calculate fake lighting based on a given vector and matrix. If you're using camera space, it can be used for a Fresnel effect. Be aware that if you're using camera space, the baked channel will be static. Ambient Occlusion ¶ Ambient occlusion will create a dark color around the corner area for the objects. This layer is heavy to use, so it's better to bake it as an image after you finish tweaking the settings. Edge Detect ¶ Edge detect will add white color around the edge proximity of the mesh. Like the Ambient Occlusion layer, this is a heavy realtime layer to use, so it's better to bake it as an image if you finish tweaking the settings. Adjustment ¶ Adjustment layer is actually just a layer that uses the previous layer as the source data, then it will add a modifier on top of it. More explanation can be found in the modifier page . Texture ¶ You can use Blender's generated textures as a layer, for example Noise , Magic , Brick , Voronoi , etc. Bake to Layer Types ¶ You can use a baked texture as a layer, for example AO, Cavity, Bevel. Be aware that the baking process may take a while to finish, depending on your system and settings. Various bake-to-layer types are explained here . Group ¶ Group layer can combine several layers into one layer and add a mask or a modifier on top of it. This can be really slow if you're using many layers and channels at the same time. Layer group demo Layer List Options ¶ This feature is currently still experimental, but you can make the layer list cleaner with layer list options. Layer list options demo The options for layer list options are: Expandable Subitems : Enabling this will make layers with masks or custom data expandable. When you click the subitems (Mask or custom channel data), it will make the mask/custom data active. Inline Subitems : Enabling this will make the item in the layer list show only one data. This option can only be enabled if Expandable Subitems is enabled.

docs.text: Layer Channel ¶ The layer channel is a bridge between layers and channels. You can choose which channel(s) your layer will affect. Layer channel blending ¶ By default, you’ll get the option to change the blending mode of the channel you select when you create the new layer. Changing blending mode of default enabled channel Layer channel panel ¶ You can do more than blending for the layer channel, if you click the triangle, you'll see all the channel options. Layer channel panel has multiple levels of UI dropdown Every channel that you can use in a layer has its own blending, sources, and modifier stacks. Layer channels legends Enabling layer channel(s) ¶ To enable the channel in a layer, you can just tick the checkbox toggle beside the channel. You can enable multiple channels at the same time, and the default value that contributes to the channel is the layer color. Enabling multiple layer channels Change layer channel source ¶ By default, the layer color is the data that is used to contribute to the channel, but you can change the source to a different data. Change layer channel source to use custom value ¶ For multiple channels in a single layer, one of the most useful sources is a custom value, it will change the painted area to use only a single value, useful to set the metallic and roughness of the painted area independently. Change layer channel source to custom value Change layer channel source to use custom data ¶ Other than a custom value, you can also use custom data for the channel source. Custom data that you can choose Custom data can be an image, color attribute, or textures. Changing layer channel source to use noise Layer channel options ¶ Options for color layer channel Channel panel in a layer has various options depending on the channel type. All channel types have at least these options: Opacity : Opacity of the layer channel. The value will be multiplied by the layer's opacity. Blend : Blend type of the layer channel Use Clamp : Clamp the value of the layer channel to 0.0 minimum and 1.0 maximum value Source : Source for the layer channel, by default, it uses the layer's color value. Height layer channel options ¶ Height layer channel has extra options. Those are: Scale : Height scale in object space. Midlevel : The baseline value to define the zero height. By default, it uses 0.5 (gray) value, which means white color will become bumps, and black color will become creases. Use As Normal Only : Enabling this will convert the height channel to a normal channel, which means the height bump value will be blended through the normal channel Normal layer channel options ¶ Normal layer channel has extra options. Those are: Strength : Strength of the normal. Space : Normal space that will be used. Vector Displacement layer channel options ¶ Strength : Strength of the vector displacement. Flip Y/Z : Some VDM maps can have different which axis pointing upward, so flip Y/Z can be useful to switch the axis. Special alpha layer channel behavior ¶ Alpha channel is a special channel that is paired with the color channel. If the color channel is enabled in a layer, the alpha channel will also be enabled and the individual options of opacity and blending will disappear and will follow the color channel instead Load PBR images ¶ Using custom data, especially images, can be useful to assign each channel to the respective image from PBR image texture packs. There are a lot of sites that you can use to download PBR texture images, like ambientCG or Poly Haven . You can either use Open Image to load an image as a layer channel custom data one by one, or you can automatically assign images to the respective channel by choosing Open Images as Single Layer when creating a new layer. Open Images as Single Layer menu when creating a new layer Open images as single layer automatically detects suffixes in the image filename to determine which image corresponds to which channel. Ucupaint assigns channels based on whether the channel name (or any of its synonyms) appears at the end of the image filename. Because using both sometimes can produce an exaggerated, doubled normal effect in many PBR image sets, Ucupaint includes a Height/Normal Map Priority option to control which one should be used. So make sure your material is using actual images rather than procedural nodes.

docs.text: Mapping ¶ Mapping defines how a layer/mask is projected onto the mesh. Ucupaint provides several mapping methods, each using a different coordinate system to determine how the layer/mask is applied to the surface. By default, layers and masks use UV mapping. Mapping controls ¶ Most mapping methods provide controls to adjust the mapping position and orientation, including offset, rotation, scale, and transform vector. Decal mapping is the only mapping method that does not provide these transform controls. Default Menu The mapping panel includes the following configurable parameters. Coordinate : Select the mapping method. See mapping methods below. UV Map : Only available for UV Map coordinate. Specifies the UV map of the object that will be used. Projection Blend : Only available for Generated and Object coordinates. It's to blend the textures around the projection corners. Transform : Specifies the transformation space or type. Offset : Shifts the position on the texture across an axis. Rotation : Rotates the texture orientation. Scale : Scales the texture along an axis. Blur : Applies a noise blur filter to the mapping vector. You need to increase the sample value if you want to bake the layer/mask/node. Other than decal, the rest of the coordinate types have Transform, Offset, Rotation, and Scale controls. Coordinate Types ¶ To illustrate the mapping coordinate types, the examples use the same image to demonstrate how it is projected onto the mesh. Texture used for example Generated ¶ Generated mapping projects the layer/mask around the mesh from all directions using coordinates generated from its geometry, creating a box-like projection around the object. Generated Normal ¶ Normal mapping projects the layer/mask onto the mesh using the direction of its surface normals, creating a projection that follows the orientation of the surface. Normal UV ¶ UV mapping projects the layer/mask onto the mesh using its UV coordinates, allowing the layer/mask to follow the existing UV layout of the object. UV Object ¶ Object mapping projects the layer/mask using the mesh's coordinates in Blender's 3D space, creating a three-dimensional projection around the object. Object Camera ¶ Camera mapping projects the layer/mask onto the mesh from the camera's viewpoint, creating a projection that follows the camera's position and orientation. Camera Window ¶ Window mapping projects the layer/mask onto the mesh using screen-space coordinates, similar to cutting out a picture in the shape of the mesh from the background. Window Reflection ¶ Reflection mapping projects the layer/mask onto the mesh using reflection directions calculated from the camera and the surface normals, similar to reflecting a ray off a reflective surface to determine where the texture is sampled. Reflection Decal ¶ Decal mapping projects the layer/mask onto the mesh using a defined projection shape. After selecting decal coordinate mapping, Ucupaint will spawn an empty object that will control the decal. By default, it's parented to the active object. The Decal method is an exception and does not provide Transform, Offset, Scale, or Rotate options. Instead, it possesses the following options: Decal Object : Points to the object in the scene to use as decal projection. By default, it points to the spawned empty object, but can be replaced by any other object. Mode : Chooses from decal projection methods (Flat, Cylinder, Sphere) Scale : Only available for Cylinder and Sphere Decal. It provides scaling for the image X and Y across the decal projection, allowing for repetition or cropping of the decal projected part. Decal constraint : Only available for flat decal. Applies constraints to surface modifier, pulling decal to be always on surface of the object. Decal Distance : Controls how far the texture is projected. Select Decal Object : A button that automatically selects the decal object. Set Position to cursor : Sets the 3d space cursor to the decal position. Plane Decal ¶ Plane decal mapping projects the layer/mask from a flat plane onto the mesh, similar to projecting an image straight onto a surface. Decal plane Cylinder ¶ Cylinder decal mapping projects the layer/mask from the inside of a cylinder onto the mesh, like placing the image on the inside of a tube and projecting it onto the object. Decal cylinder Sphere ¶ Sphere decal mapping projects the layer/mask from the inside of a sphere onto the mesh, like placing the image on the inside of a ball and projecting it onto the object. Decal sphere

docs.text: Mask ¶ Masks can be useful to hide or show certain parts of a layer. It uses the value 1.0 (white) as visible and 0.0 (black) as transparent. You can access layer masks below the layer channels. Layer masks panel Add New Mask ¶ To add a new mask, just press the '+' button and you'll be given an options menu with many mask types. More details about layer mask types can be accessed here . You can add as many masks as you like in a single layer, and they don't have to be using the same mask types. New layer mask menu New Image Mask Options ¶ If you choose Image > New Image , a dialog box will appear. New image mask dialog box Most of the options are similar to new image layers options , with some exceptions: Color : Color of the mask, white for full opacity and black for full transparency. Blend : Blending of the mask, the default is Multiply , which means the mask will be multiplied to the layer alpha value. Painting an Image Mask ¶ Painting an image mask is as simple as painting black to hide and painting white to reveal the layer. This is a very useful way to non-destructively manipulate your layer. Adding and painting image masks UI related to Mask ¶ If a layer has one or two masks, more icons will be visible in the layer list, and there will be an icon to enable/disable all masks assigned to the layer. Explanation of mask-related UI Every mask their own of blending, opacity, and visibility toggle. Mask visibility and opacity demo The icon button between the mask opacity and mask menu is used to set the active data that will be used for painting (if the mask is an image) or editing (if the mask is a color attribute or color ID). It can also be used for previewing the data (more info in the Preview Mode page) Switching active data between masks and layer Mask Menu ¶ Mask menu contain various operators, like for reordering the masks, merging, removing, baking, and adding modifier specific the the mask. Menu for reordering masks and other things Baking a mask as an image ¶ Baking a mask as an image is available in the mask menu. It will bake all kinds of masks with its mapping to an image. Bake mask as image has some special options Bake mask as an image has similar options to baking data to a layer/mask . But it has extra options: Use Blur : Add blur to the baked image. It uses compositing nodes, so the blur result is much cleaner than using blur in the mapping options. Duplicate Mask : The bake result will become a new separate mask. Disable Current Mask : Only shows if Duplicate Mask is enabled. This will make the original mask disabled after baking. After you bake a mask as an image (unless you choose to duplicate the mask), you can switch back to the original unbaked data. Baked data information and some buttons will appear after baking The screenshot above is an example of noise mask baked as an image. Notice that all the noise parameters and mappings are greyed out if you use the baked image. There's also a button to rebake and remove the baked image data. Mask Blending ¶ Other than setting the opacity and blend types, there are also options for the mask to only affect specific channels. Mask blending panel If you notice in the screenshot above, there are some channels that have darker texts, that means those channels aren't enabled in the layer. There are many benefits of baking a mask to an image. Some of them are: Improve performance for Blender's generated textures (Noise, Voronoi, etc.) since images have much faster performance than procedural textures Adding blur to a Color ID mask will make it possible to be usable for the height channel. Mask Orders ¶ Be aware that mask order in the mask panel is different than the layer list order. In the layer list, the blending is calculated from bottom to top, but in the mask panel, mask blending is calculated from top to bottom. The reason for this is that layer data is placed above the mask panel, and the first mask will be blended to the layer's alpha value, so the order makes more sense for it to be from top to bottom. Mask Types ¶ Ucupaint’s mask types are mostly the same as its layer types , with a few exceptions. Color ID ¶ Color ID will use a unique random color ID that will work as a mask. It uses a color attribute named __yp_color_id to store its color ID, when the color IDs match, it will be valued 1.0, otherwise it will be valued at 0.0. Like the color attribute, Ucupaint has a special editor to easily edit color IDs in edit mode. Color ID mask Demo Object Index ¶ Object Index will mask objects with the same index. It's useful if one material is used with many objects. Make sure to expand the Object & Material panel to check the index of the selected object. Object Index Masks Demo Backface ¶ Backface will mask out the backface of the surface. WARNING: This mask type can't be baked .

docs.text: Modifier ¶ Modifiers are useful to add non-destructive effects. You can apply modifiers to a layer, a mask, or the layer channel. Various Add Modifier menu locations Keep in mind that not all modifier types are available for every item type. For example, there are only three modifiers available for masks (Invert, Ramp, and Curve). Adding modifier to a layer, a layer channel, and a mask Modifier types ¶ Invert : will invert selected RGB and alpha values RGB to Alpha : will convert the RGB of your layer to intensity/alpha and replace the layer's RGB values with a single color. Alpha to RGB : will convert the alpha of your layer to RGB and replace the layer's alpha value itself with a solid value Color Ramp : will map the layer RGB values to a color ramp RGB Curve : will tweak the RGB values using a curve Hue Saturation : will tweak the RGB values using hue and saturation parameters Brightness Contrast : will tweak the RGB values using brightness and contrast parameters Math : will tweak the RGB and alpha values using math operations Modifier orders ¶ Be aware if you have more than one modifier, modifier order will affect the result. The order is from bottom to top, so the top modifier will be executed last. You can edit modifier order using this menu. Menu for reordering modifier Adjustment Layer ¶ If you create a new layer, there's an option to create an adjustment layer. An adjustment layer actually uses a layer type called Previous Layers with a modifier applied. The modifier applied to the Previous Layers layer will be applied to the all previous layers of the current layer and it will be applied to all channels selected on the layer. Adjustment Layer Demo Transition Modifiers ¶ Transition modifiers are special modifiers that are applied to the layer alpha (including masks) gradient value. It applied on the layer channel but will also affect other channels. Transition Bump ¶ Transition bump can be only added to a Height layer channel, it's to sharpen the alpha transition, very useful to create bump lines. Transition Bump Demo Options for transition bump are: Max Height : Height of the transition bump. The layer height's midlevel will be at the level of the transition bump max height. Edge 1 : The sharpness of the outer edge of the alpha gradient Edge 2 : The sharpness of the inner edge of the alpha gradient Affected Masks : Number of masks that the transition bump will be applied to Flip : Flip the transition bump height, this will produce a different effect than just using a negative value of the max height Crease : Add crease at the outside of the transition bump effect (Can only be used if Flip is disabled) Falloff : Add falloff to the alpha gradient falloff. On other channels than height, a Transition Factor will appear to control the sharpness of the alpha transition of that specific channel. Transition Ramp ¶ Transition ramp is for adding a ramp modifier along the alpha gradient value. The transition ramp effect will be sharper if there is also a transition bump enabled in the height channel. Transition Ramp Demo Options for the transition ramp are: Opacity : Opacity of the transition ramp Blend : Blend type of the transition ramp There's an extra option in the gear button called Unlink Ramp with Channel Intensity , it's for unpairing the channel opacity value with the transition ramp colors, so the layer channel can be transparent, but the transition ramp will still be opaque. Transition AO ¶ Transition AO is for adding a fake ambient occlusion effect in the area outside of the transition bump. You need the transition bump to be enabled on the height first to use Transition AO. Transition AO Demo Options for transition AO are: Opacity : Opacity of the transition AO Blend : Blend type of the transition AO Power : Strength of the AO Color : Color of the AO Inside : Will also add AO inside the inner part of the transition bump

docs.text: Maximum images per Material in Blender ¶ If you exceed the number of images, material in Blender can appear pink in the viewport. The number of image limit varies across machine specifications and Blender versions. Here are some limitations found. Use unique Image Atlas per Ucupaint node tree : Use a unique image atlas per Ucupaint node tree rather than every node using the same image atlas. docs.text: Export and Import Layers to PSD file ¶ Warning Currently, the export/import layers feature is available only in Ucupaint Plus, which you can get by becoming at least a silver GitHub sponsor Ucupaint Plus supports exporting and importing layer data to and from PSD files. This feature lets you save your layers in a format compatible with other image editors that use PSD. Export Layers to PSD ¶ To export layers as PSD, press the special menu button beside the layer list (the one with the V icon), and choose Export Layers as PSD . Export layers to PSD button Then the export dialog box will appear. Export layers to PSD dialog box Ucupaint uses PSD-Tools module to make PSD import and export work, so Ucupaint will download the module the first time you do PSD export/import. The necessary space needed is about 50-80MB, so the download process might take a couple of seconds to minutes, depending on your internet connection. There are two options for the export, the first one is Channel , which only layers that use that channel will be exported. The second option is Convert Solid Colors to pixels , this converts solid color layers to standard pixel layers. This is useful since not all 2D applications can read color fill layers from a PSD file (example: Gimp). The comparison below shows the exported layers as shown in Photopea. Convert Solid Colors to pixels disabled Convert Solid Colors to pixels enabled Import Layers from PSD ¶ To import layers from a PSD file, you only need to open the image as a layer. And there will be a menu to read the layers if you select a PSD file. Open image as layer Read Photoshop layers will show up when you select a PSD file The option Convert Flat Layer to Solid Color will detect the standard pixel image, and if the values are the same for all the pixels, it will be converted to a solid color layer. Limitations ¶ Only layers with types of Image , Solid Color , or Group are currently supported for export PSD can only have one mask per layer, so only one image mask is supported for export Adjustment layers are not supported yet Modifiers from ucupaint are also not supported yet Tips ¶ If the color or the blending looks weird on your 2D app. Check the actual color by enabling the color channel's Preview Mode . And if it still looks too different, you can also try to disable Use Linear Color Blending . By disabling that, the blending colors between layers will be more similar to Photoshop. Use Linear Color Blending should be disabled to make the blending in ucupaint look the same as in Photoshop Video Demo ¶ You can watch the PSD layers export-import demo on YouTube . docs.text: Ucupaint Setup ¶ Before Setting Up Ucupaint ¶ Assuming you've already installed the addon. The Ucupaint tab will appear in the N-panel when an object is selected. Before you continue, make sure to check the following: Make sure you are in Material Preview mode Make sure your object has been properly unwrapped Even though this addon supports more than just mesh objects, some features, such as baking operations, will only work with mesh objects . Creating The Ucupaint Node ¶ Ucupaint is a node group. You can create a new Ucupaint node directly in the Shader Editor. Creating new Ucupaint node in the Shader Editor In the Shader Editor, press Shift + A, go to Group, and select Ucupaint to add the node to your material. When adding a Ucupaint node in the Shader Editor, it will start with a single channel: Color. You can connect the Color output to any other node in your shader as needed. More details about channels are explained in channel page . Quick Setup ¶ You can also quickly set up the Ucupaint node in the 3D viewport by clicking the "Quick Ucupaint Node Setup" button. Quick setup button A pop-up menu will appear, giving you a few options for setting up the node. You can choose different shader types and add various channels. Quick setup options Here are the options available in the Quick Setup menu: Tree Name : The name of the Ucupaint node group (tree). Toggle the icon on the right to set the material name as the Ucupaint tree name. Type : The BSDF shader type that the Ucupaint node will connect to. Channels : The default set of channels included in the node (additional channels can be added later). Use Linear Color Blending : Enables linear blending between layers. This is more color-accurate but behaves differently than traditional 2D software like Photoshop. Use ORM Bake Target : Use ORM format that packs Ambient Occlusion, Roughness, and Metallic channels into a single bake target image (this can save baking time) Switch to Material View : Automatically changes the viewport shading to Material View after setup. The OK button completes the setup process. Ucupaint is now ready to use, and the channels, along with the layer list, will be visible. Ucupaint is now ready to use! If you open the shader editor, the quick setup creates a group node connected to the default shader (Principled BSDF), based on the channels you selected earlier. Avoid editing the contents of this group node manually, as it may cause critical errors. What quick setup actually creates Linking Ucupaint Node Tree ¶ If you already have a node tree in the shader editor, the Ucupaint node will be placed between your existing nodes and the shader. It will automatically connect the existing channels through the Ucupaint node, keeping your current setup intact and working as before. See the video below for a demonstration. Linking Ucupaint Node Tree with Existing Node setup Expand/Collapse Menu ¶ Ucupaint’s UI may look simple at first, but it offers more options hidden within collapsible menus. Whenever you see a small triangle or arrow next to a section, it indicates that more settings can be expanded. You can see this behavior in the example GIF below. Expand and collapse additional options menus Node Gear Menu ¶ At the top right of Ucupaint, there's a gear icon that, when clicked, shows various functions for the active node. Ucupaint node gear menu The operators and options in the menu are: Bake Ucupaint Node : Bake Ucupaint node to what is specified in the bake targets. This option is the same button on the bake target popover, so it's only available for Blender 2.7x or if you enabled non-popup UI in user preferences. Rename Ucupaint Node Tree : This will rename the Ucupaint node tree group Remove Ucupaint Node : This will delete the active Ucupaint Node and remove all the layers and its data, except the final baked data. Clean Ucupaint Caches : Ucupaint sometimes store some custom images and nodes for caching, this function is to remove them all Duplicate Material and Ucupaint Nodes : To duplicate the material and Ucupaint node for the active object. Active Node Tree : You can use more than one ucupaint nodes in a material, so this menu is to switch between them. Use Linear Color Blending : If disabled , blending between layers will happen in gamma space, which mimics how default Photoshop behaves. Stats : Shows how many images, color attributes, and other data have the node already been used.

Ucupaint Plus Roadmap ¶ Roadmap for Ucupaint Plus, which is available for at least silver sponsors on GitHub . Some of these features will probably eventually come to regular ucupaint if the funding goes well. Feature Status Planned for version Comments PSD file export-import Done 2.4.7 Krita KRA file export-import WIP 3.x Gimp XCF file export-import WIP 3.x Sync External File No 3.x if the first goal achieved for GitHub Sponsors Sync external layered files like PSD, KRA, or XCF so if you edited the file in Blender or an outside application, there is a way to sync between those two. (#358) Multiple decals in a single layer/mask No #396 Mirrored decal option No #270 Vector/Coordinate warp Testing Manipulating vector mapping using images/attributes/generated textures. (#96) Multi-material batch baking No Probably will be implemented alongside #77 Baking multiple maps at the same time (AO, Pointiness, etc.) No #399 Multi-user node group support No #398 Lock layers No #199 Passthrough Group No #134 Copy paste modifier No #89 Duplicate mask No #153 Option to apply baked layer/mask as standard image No #313 Reimplement parallax No #397 Principled BSDF layering support No #353 Normal map-aware edge detect Not sure if possible Use Blender layer backend Not possible yet Since Blender already plans to create a native layer system. If that’s implemented, it will be better to use that as the backend of Ucupaint. Ucupaint 3.0 ¶ Ucupaint 3.0 implemented a lot of internal refactors and some UI redesigns to make it easier to navigate. Separating them requires a lot of refactoring, but it is worth it to avoid unnecessary complexity in the future. (#323) Base layer Done For less confusion, Ucupaint node inputs will be accessible as a base layer rather than channel settings. It’s useful for adjusting the channel value in the middle of the layer stack. Make sure useful features like preview mode are still accessible with the panel collapsed. (#395) Rename Vector input to Mapping Done In Ucupaint, Vector makes more sense if renamed to Mapping . docs.text: Performance Tips ¶ Here are some performance tips while using ucupaint Use fewer generated textures, like noise or voronoi, if you want the shader compilation to be faster If you still want many generated textures, it's better to bake them as an image since the material performance will be a lot faster. The option to Bake Mask as Image is inside the gear button beside the mask. If you get lag after doing a brushstroke, it's probably because Blender wants to refresh the material preview image, so closing the material panel that shows the preview will likely make the lag go away. Using Sculpt Mode to paint a color attribute layer/mask will have better performance than using Vertex Paint Mode

docs.text: Transfer UV ¶ Transfer UV can be useful when you need to transfer an image from one UV map to another UV map. This can be useful if your original UV map wasn't very good and you already created a better one. The transfer process can take a while since it uses Blender's baking system. Transfer UV is accessible beside the UV Map section in the expanded mapping panel. Transfer UV menu There are two operators that you can choose, Transfer UV will only transfer the current image layer/mask, while Transfer All Layers & Masks UV will transfer all image layers/masks that use the same UV. The Transfer UV operator options are: From UV : Only available for Transfer All Layers & Masks UV . All image layers and masks that use this UV will be transferred to new UV. Target UV / To UV : The target UV that the image will be transferred into. Samples : Samples for the transferred image, the default is using one sample. It's generally fine, but try to increase it if the bake result has jagged lines or noise. Margin : Number of color pixels spread along the edge of UV islands to hide the UV seams, please increase it if the seam of your model looks visible in the far distance. Delete From UV : Only available for Transfer All Layers & Masks UV . Selected UV on From UV will be deleted after the transfer process is done. Useful if you don't want to use the original UV anymore. Demo ¶ For example, we can transfer an image from the original UV ( UVMap ) where the image is painted to other UV ( UVMap.001 ).
